verses.text: Listen to me, you islands. Pay attention, you peoples far away. The LORD called me before I was born. He said my name while I was still inside my mother.
He made my mouth like a sharp sword and hid me in the shadow of his hand. He made me a polished arrow and kept me tucked in his quiver.
He told me, “You’re my servant, Israel. I’ll show my glory through you.”
But I said, “I’ve worked for nothing. I burned through my strength for nothing at all. Still, the justice I’m owed is with the LORD, and my reward is with my God.”
Now the LORD has spoken, the one who shaped me from the womb to serve him, to bring Jacob back and gather Israel to him. I matter in the LORD’s eyes, and my God has become my strength.

He says, “Bringing up Jacob’s tribes and bringing back the survivors of Israel is too small a job for my servant. I’ll make you a light for the nations too, so my salvation reaches the ends of the earth.”

Here’s what the LORD, Israel’s Redeemer and Holy One, says to the one people look down on, the one the nation can’t stand, the servant of rulers: “Kings will see you and get up from their seats. Princes will bow down in worship because the LORD is faithful. The Holy One of Israel has chosen you.”

The LORD says, “I answered you when the time was right. I helped you on the day of salvation. I’ll keep you safe and make you a covenant for the people, to restore the land and hand them back their abandoned inheritance.
You’ll say to the people in chains, ‘Come out!’ and to the ones in darkness, ‘Let yourselves be seen!’ They’ll feed along the roads, and even the bare hills will be pasture for them.
They won’t get hungry or thirsty. The heat and sun won’t beat them down, because the one who shows them mercy will lead them and guide them to springs of water.
I’ll turn all my mountains into roads, and my highways will be raised up.
Look, here they come from far away. Here are some from the north, some from the west, and some from the land of Sinim.”
Sing, heavens! Celebrate, earth! Break into song, mountains! The LORD has comforted his people, and he’ll have compassion on the ones who are hurting.
But Zion said, “The LORD walked away from me. The Lord forgot about me.”
“Could a woman forget the baby she’s nursing? Could she stop caring about the child she carried? Even if she does forget, I won’t forget you!
Look, I’ve carved you into the palms of my hands. Your walls are always in front of me.
Your children are hurrying back. The people who ruined you and left you wrecked will leave you.
Look up. Look all around. They’re gathering and coming to you. As surely as I live,” says the LORD, “you’ll wear them like jewelry and dress yourself up with them like a bride.
“Your ruins, your empty places, and the land that was wrecked will be too small for all the people living there. The ones who swallowed you up will be far away.
The children you have after your loss will say right in your hearing, ‘It’s too crowded here. Make some room for me to live.’
Then you’ll say to yourself, ‘Who had these children for me? I lost my children and was left alone, an exile wandering from place to place. Who raised all these? I was on my own. Where were they?’”
The Lord GOD says, “Look, I’ll lift my hand to the nations and raise my banner for the peoples. They’ll bring your sons held close against their chests and carry your daughters on their shoulders.

Kings will be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. They’ll bow till their faces touch the ground and lick the dust at your feet. Then you’ll know I’m the LORD. The people who wait for me won’t be let down.”
Can you take plunder back from somebody powerful? Can you free the captives they’re entitled to hold?
But the LORD says, “Even the captives of the mighty will be taken back. Loot will be snatched from the fierce. I’ll fight the ones fighting you, and I’ll save your children.
I’ll feed your oppressors their own flesh. They’ll get drunk on their own blood like it’s sweet wine. Then everybody will know I’m the LORD, your Savior and Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.”
